mmm.note: Shows you like a taste or smell, or that you are thinking: "Mmm, good!"
ex: Mmm, this soup is really good.
Mmm, can I have another piece of cake?
Mmm, that smells great. What are you cooking?
Mmm, let me think about it for a minute.

link.say: click on a link · send a link
link.note: Often "link" means a connection: "a link between sleep and health."
ex: Can you send me the link, please?
Click on the link to buy tickets.
This link doesn't work. Can you check it?
I put the link to the video in the chat.

trailer.say: watch a trailer · the trailer for a movie
trailer.note: Also means a vehicle pulled behind a car or truck.
ex: Have you seen the trailer for the new movie?
The trailer looks good. Let's watch the movie.
They show a lot of trailers before the film.
We put our bikes in a small trailer behind the car.

final.say: in the final · watch the final
final.note: Most often "final" means last: "my final answer." In the US, "finals" are also end-of-year exams.
ex: Are you going to watch the final tonight?
Our team is in the final this year!
They lost the final by one goal.
The tickets for the final are very expensive.

market.say: at the market · on the market
market.note: Most often "market" means buying and selling: "the job market," "the stock market."
ex: I need to go to the market for milk.
Is there a market near your hotel?
The little market on our street opens at seven.
Can you buy some bread at the market?

opera.say: go to the opera · at the opera
ex: Do you want to go to the opera tonight?
We have two tickets for the opera on Saturday.
She sings opera in Italian and French.
The opera starts at seven, so don't be late.
We need oxygen to breathe and live.
The doctor gave him oxygen through a mask.
Trees and plants give us oxygen every day.
There is less oxygen high in the mountains.

character.note: Most often "character" means a person in a story or film: "my favorite character."
ex: My sister has a strong character and never gives up.
The two brothers look the same but have different characters.
Hard work at school can build character.
Her calm character helps a lot in difficult times.

tennis.note: No article: "play tennis," not "play the tennis."

drama.note: Informal: "drama" also means silly fights between people: "Stop the drama!"
ex: Do you like comedies or dramas more?
My daughter takes drama classes after school.
We watched a new crime drama on TV last night.
This film is a sad drama about a family.

formula.note: In the US, "formula" is also milk powder for babies.

chill.note: Slang for "relax," often "chill out." Most often "chill" means cold: "a chill in the air."
ex: Let's just chill at home tonight.
I want to chill after work today.
Do you want to chill at my place?
We chilled by the pool all afternoon.

motor.note: For cars, people usually say "engine": "The car has a new engine."
ex: The boat has a small motor at the back.
The motor in my washing machine stopped working.
This fan has a very quiet motor.
Can you fix the motor, or do I need a new one?

strike.note: Most often "strike" is a verb meaning to hit: "Lightning struck the tree."
ex: The workers are on strike again this week.
Is there a train strike tomorrow?
The teachers went on strike for better pay.
Because of the strike, the buses are not running.

info.note: Informal and uncountable: some info (not "an info"). The full word is "information."
ex: Thanks for the info, it really helps.
Can you send me more info about the job?
I need some info about the trip.
You can find more info on our website.

assist.note: Most often "assist" is a formal verb meaning help: "Can I assist you?"
ex: He scored one goal and made two assists.
She had five assists in the last game.
That was a great assist from the captain!
Who made the assist for the first goal?

specialist.say: see a specialist · a specialist in

ex: She doesn't wear much makeup to work.
Take off your makeup before you go to bed.
Where can I buy good makeup for sensitive skin?
It takes me ten minutes to put on makeup.

cable.say: a charging cable · plug in a cable
cable.note: In the US, "cable" also means cable TV: "We don't have cable."
ex: Do you have a phone cable I can use?
This cable is too short for my laptop.
Plug the cable into the back of the TV.
I need a new charging cable for my phone.

hall.note: Often "hall" means a big room or building: "a concert hall," "the town hall."
ex: Please wait for me in the hall downstairs.
You can leave your shoes in the hall.
We hung our coats in the front hall.
Is there a mirror in the hall?

hockey.note: In American English "hockey" means ice hockey.

accent.say: a strong accent · speak with an accent
ex: She speaks English with a strong French accent.
I love your accent. Where are you from?
My accent is not perfect, but people understand me.
It is hard to lose an accent as an adult.
This computer has very cheap components inside.
One component of the machine is broken.
Each component comes in a separate box.
Check every component before you start the job.

pirate.note: Also a person who copies films or music illegally.
ex: The pirates attacked the ship at night.
My son wants to dress up as a pirate.
We read a book about pirates and gold.
The movie is about a famous pirate captain.

coach.say: a life coach · a business coach
coach.note: Most often "coach" means a sports trainer: "Our coach makes us run a lot."
ex: She works as a life coach for busy parents.
My business coach helps me plan my week.
I hired a career coach to find a new job.
Do you think a coach can help me speak better?

portrait.say: paint a portrait · a portrait of

context.say: in this context · out of context
ex: Guess the meaning of the word from the context.
Read the whole text to understand the context.
This word has a different meaning in this context.
Can you give me some context? I don't understand.
He likes his whiskey with a little ice.
This whiskey is twelve years old.
Can I have a glass of whiskey, please?
We had a whiskey together after dinner.

retreat.say: go on a retreat · a yoga retreat
retreat.note: Often "retreat" means to move back, away from danger: "The army had to retreat."
ex: We are going on a yoga retreat in the mountains.
Our company has a team retreat every spring.
She spent a week at a quiet retreat by the lake.
How much does the weekend retreat cost?

organ.note: Also a big musical instrument in a church: "She plays the organ."
ex: The heart is a very important organ.
He needs a new organ from a donor.
The liver is the largest organ inside the body.
Smoking can damage many organs in your body.

critic.say: a film critic · a food critic
critic.note: A critic is a person; the article or opinion is a review.
ex: The critics loved the new film.
She works as a food critic for a magazine.
The critic gave the movie four stars.
My dad is always my biggest critic.

track.say: a track on the album · a race track
track.note: Often "track" means a path or rails: "a train track," "keep track of time."
ex: This is the best track on the album.
Can you send me the name of this track?
The runners go around the track four times.
I listen to this track every morning.

euro.note: Say "a euro," not "an euro": it starts with a "you" sound.
ex: The museum ticket costs fifty euros.
The euro is used in many countries.
Can I pay in euros or only in dollars?
How many euros do I need for the trip?

don.note: Most often "Don" is a man's name. "To don" means to put on clothes (formal).

scandal.say: a big scandal · a scandal about
scandal.note: Not used for a loud family fight; say "a fight" or "an argument."

democrat.note: In the US, usually with a capital D for the political party.
ex: My parents have always been Democrats.
She is a Democrat and votes in every election.
The Democrats have a new plan for schools.
He is a true democrat and respects every vote.

operator.say: a tour operator · a machine operator
operator.note: In the US, a phone company is usually a "carrier," not an "operator."
ex: Call the operator if you need help.
He works as a machine operator in a factory.
Our tour operator booked a nice hotel for us.
The operator told me to wait for a minute.

minimum.say: a minimum of · to a minimum
ex: The minimum age for this job is 18.
You need a minimum of two hours for this.
Please keep the noise to a minimum after ten.
What is the minimum price for this car?

finish.say: the finish line · a close finish
finish.note: Most often "finish" is a verb meaning to end: "I finish work at six."
ex: She ran all the way to the finish line.
The race had a very exciting finish.
Let's wait for the runners at the finish.
It was a close finish between the two cars.

veteran.note: Also means a person with long experience: a veteran teacher.

ex: The jet flew low over the city.
He flies to work in his private jet.
The jet landed safely in the rain.
We could hear the noise of a jet above.

comrade.note: Sounds old or political today; "friend" or "fellow soldier" is more common.

trauma.note: Only for serious harm. For a small hurt, like a knee or sports injury, say "injury."
ex: He had head trauma after the car accident.
The war caused deep trauma for many people.
She sees a therapist to deal with her trauma.
Many children need help after this kind of trauma.

reply.say: get a reply · in reply to
reply.note: Often "reply" is a verb: "Please reply to my email."
ex: Thanks for your quick reply to my email.
I'm still waiting for a reply from the bank.
Her funny reply got a lot of likes.
Read the replies under my post.

humor.note: Uncountable: "a sense of humor." British spelling is "humour."

ex: We need an investor for our small business.
The investors liked our idea very much.
He puts his money in tech as a small investor.
She has a meeting with two investors today.
The movie has very funny dialogue.
We practiced a short dialogue in English class.
The two countries started a dialogue about peace.
Open dialogue between parents and kids is important.

venture.say: a business venture · a joint venture
venture.note: As a verb, "venture" means to go somewhere risky: "venture outside."
ex: Their new business venture is doing very well.
Opening a small cafe was a risky venture.
The two companies started a joint venture last year.
Do you have money for a new venture?

amateur.note: Also an adjective: "an amateur photographer" (not paid, does it for fun).
ex: He is not a professional, just an amateur.
This competition is only for amateurs.
My dad is an amateur, but his photos are great.
She plays golf as an amateur on weekends.
